["guinea pig sensitization test","Induction: 2% cinnamaldehyde, 0.5 ml on gauze, 6 h occlusion, days 1,8,15; challenge: 0.75% cinnamaldehyde, 6 h occlusion, 10 guinea pigs (Dunkin-Hartley); vehicle not specified.","In a guinea pig sensitization test, induction with 2% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not specified) applied occluded for 6 h on days 1, 8, and 15 to Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs (10/group), followed by challenge with 0.75% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not specified) via 6 h occluded patch, resulted in 3 sensitization reactions and 1 questionable reaction out of 10 animals (Basketter and Allenby, 1991a)."]

["guinea pig sensitization test (photoallergy study protocol)","Induction: 0.3 ml of 200 mg/ml cinnamic acid applied to nuchal area of male hairless guinea pigs after intradermal Freund's complete adjuvant and tape stripping, occluded for 2 h, repeated on days 3,5,8,10,12. ["Guinea pig skin sensitization test (Maguire method)","Induction: 4 open topical applications of 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum (0.2 ml onto 2 cm² abraded shoulder) on days 0,2,4,7; third induction preceded by intradermal Freund's complete adjuvant at 2 sites. ["LLNA","1.0% in ethanol; 5 female Hartley albino guinea pigs","In an LLNA, cinnamaldehyde at 1.0% in ethanol stimulated lymph node cell proliferation in female Hartley albino guinea pigs."]

["guinea pig maximization test","10 female albino guinea pigs (Himalayan strain, 4 weeks old, SPF-quality) test group; 5 female guinea pigs controls; intradermally injected and epidermally exposed to undiluted D6; challenged with undiluted D6 (first challenge) and 50% and 20% D6 (second challenge); 10% sodium dodecyl sulfate pretreatment 24 hours before epidermal induction; vehicle corn oil.","Pels Rijcken studied the skin sensitization potential of D6 using the maximization test. Ten female albino guinea pigs (Himalayan strain, 4 weeks old, SPF-quality) comprised the test group, and 5 female guinea pigs served as controls (corn oil = control). The test animals were intradermally injected and epidermally exposed to undiluted D6, and the 5 control guinea pigs were treated similarly with corn oil. Approximately 24 hours prior to epidermal induction exposure, all of the animals were treated with 10% sodium dodecyl sulfate. At 2 weeks after epidermal application, all of the animals were challenged with undiluted D6 and the vehicle. One week later, the animals were subjected to a second challenge with 50% D6 and 20% D6. Following the first challenge, grade 1 skin reactions were observed among 3 test animals and 1 control animal in response to undiluted D6. After the second challenge, no reactions to 50% D6 or 20% D6 were observed. Based on the results of the second challenge phase, it was concluded that there was no evidence that D6 had caused skin hypersensitivity in guinea pigs. These results indicate a sensitization rate of 0%."]

["Quantitative mechanistic model (QMM) for Schiff base formation","Molecular weight 1457, two identical aldehyde groups; Log P = -2.5 (calculated by ACD laboratories); Sigma* values derived using method of Perrin et al.","The QMM for Schiff bases has been applied to streptomycin sulfate as follows. The aldehyde group can be simplified to the general structure (ROCH₂)2C(OH)CHO. Using the method of Perrin et al., the σ* value for the (ROCH₂)2C(OH)- group has been determined to be 1.12. Adding σ* for the H atom (0.49), a value of 1.61 has been obtained for Σσ*. Log P has been calculated by ACD laboratories to be -2.5. Inserting these values in the Schiff base QMM (pEC3 = 1.12 Σσ* + 0.42Log P - 0.62) gives a pEC3 value of 0.13 for streptomycin sulfate. The molecular weight of streptomycin is 1457, and it contains two identical aldehyde groups. Thus, the calculated EC3 value is 540%. This being well above 100%, the maximum possible test concentration, the QMM correctly predicts streptomycin sulfate to be a nonsensitizer."]

["Maximization test (Kligman)","8% (5520 µg/cm²) phenethyl propionate in petrolatum, 25 healthy male volunteers, application under occlusion to forearms for five alternate-day 48 h periods, pretreatment with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS) under occlusion, challenge patches applied to fresh sites on the back for 48 h under occlusion with 1 h pretreatment with 10% SLS, evaluated at 48 and 72 h","A maximization test according to Kligman (1966) and Kligman and Epstein (1975) was carried out with 8% (5520 µg/cm²) phenethyl propionate in petrolatum on 25 healthy male volunteers. Application was under occlusion to the same site on the forearms of all subjects for five-alternate day 48 h periods. The patch sites were pretreated for 24 h with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS) under occlusion. Following a 10 day rest period, challenge patches were applied to fresh sites on the back for 48 h under occlusion. The challenge site was pre-treated for 1 h with 10% SLS. The challenge site was evaluated at 48 and 72 h. No sensitization reactions were observed (RIFM, 1973b)."]

["Maximization test (Magnusson and Kligman)","4% (2760 µg/cm²) in petrolatum, occlusive, forearms, induction 5 alternate-day 48h periods, pretreatment with 5% aqueous SLS for 24h, challenge after 10 days, 48h occlusion on back, pretreatment with 10% SLS for 1h","A maximization test with 4% 2-phenoxyethyl isobutyrate in petrolatum (2760 µg/cm²) on 25 healthy male patients used induction with 5 alternate-day 48h occlusive patches on forearms (pretreated with 5% SLS for 24h) and challenge after 10 days on the back (48h occlusion, pretreated with 10% SLS for 1h). No sensitization reactions were observed (0/25)."]

["Maximization test (MAX)","8% (5520 µg/cm²) vetiverol in petrolatum, occlusion, 30 male volunteers, induction with five alternate-day 48-hour applications, pre-treatment with 5% aqueous SLS under occlusion for 24 h, 10-14 day rest, challenge patches under occlusion for 48 h, challenge preceded by 30 min 5% SLS on left side, no SLS on right side, petrolatum control","A MAX was conducted with 8% (5520 µg/cm²) vetiverol in petrolatum on 30 male volunteers. The test material was applied under occlusion to the same sites on volar forearms of all volunteers for five alternate day, 48-hour periods. Patch sites were pre-treated for 24 h under occlusion with 5% aqueous sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS). Following a ten-fourteen day rest period, challenge patches of all materials were applied under occlusion to fresh sites for 48 h. Challenge applications were preceded by 30 minute applications of 5% aqueous SLS on the left side while the test material without any SLS was applied on the right side. Petrolatum controls were placed on the right side on a site labeled 5. Reactions were assessed at 24 h, after removal of the challenge patch and thereafter. One reaction was observed in 1/30 volunteer, however upon biopsy and retesting, this reaction was dismissed as a low grade insignificant irritant reaction. No sensitization was observed (RIFM, 1976a)."]
